case_name: Director of Settlements, A. P. and Others v M. R. Apparao and Another
petitioner: Director of Settlements, A. P. and Others
respondent:
M. R. Apparao and Another
Supreme Court of India

20 March 2002
Appeal (Civil) 2517 of 1999
The Judgment was delivered by : G. B. Pattanaik, J.
1. This appeal by the State of Andhra Pradesh is directed against the impugned Judgment of the Division Bench of the Andhra Pradesh High Court dated 04 November 1993 in Writ Appeal No. 511 of 1993. The Division Bench of the Andhra Pradesh High Court has come to the conclusion that the rights accrued in favour of the respondents to receive interim payments u/s. 39 of the Andhra Pradesh Estates (Abolition and Conversion into Ryotwari) Act, 1948, which has already become final, the earlier Judgments of the High Court, not being assailed, the decision of the Supreme Court in the Venkatagiri's case, would not take away that right and, therefore, the respondents would be entitled to receive interim payments in accordance with the judgments in their favour.

facts: This appeal by the State of Andhra Pradesh is directed against the impugned Judgment of the Division Bench of the Andhra Pradesh High Court dated 04 November 1993 in Writ Appeal No. 511 of 1993.
The two estates called Vuyyur and Meduru, were notified under the provisions of the Estates Abolition Act, 1948 and the State Government took over the two estates.
The compensation due for the estates was notified on 20 June 1961.

The State Government realising its mistake in notifying the two estates together, issued two separate notifications under the Estates Abolition Act, on 01 October 1963 and compensation for the two estates were determined separately, one on 21 November 1964 for Meduru and another on 05 April 1966 for Vuyyur.
The State Government issued an administrative instruction in G.O.Ms. No. 645 dated 28 May 1966, indicating the procedure for determining the final compensation.

A writ petition was filed in the Andhra Pradesh High Court by Raja of Venkatagiri, questioning the validity of the ordinance as well as the amendment Act and by Judgment dated 22 September 1971, the High Court declared that Act 3/1971 to the extent it extinguished the vested right of the estate holders to receive interim compensation till the date of commencement of the Act was ultra vires of Art. 31(2) and not protected by Article 31A or 31B.

The present respondents along with several others filed writ petitions before the Andhra Pradesh High Court, seeking interim payments, which were registered as Writ Petition Nos. 3293 and 3294 of 1975.

A learned Single Judge of the High Court disposed of the two writ petitions by Judgment dated 17 June 1977 and following the earlier Judgment in Venkatagiri's case, issued a writ of mandamus to make interim payments to the respondents herein in accordance with law laid down in Venkatagiri's case.
The Judgment of the Andhra Pradesh High Court in Venkatagiri's case had been assailed in the Supreme Court in Civil Appeal Nos. 398 and 1385 of 1972.
Those two appeals were disposed of by order dated 06 February 1986.

In this Court the counsel appearing for the respondents, who were the original writ petitioners before the High Court consented to the Judgments and orders of the High Court under appeal being set aside, leaving it open to the land-holders and others to get the compensation and interim payments in accordance with the amended provisions of the Andhra Pradesh (Andhra Area) Estates (Abolition and Conversion into Ryotwari) Act, 1948.
The Court also itself expressed its opinion and held that the amendments made to the Act are constitutionally valid and the view expressed in the writ petition No. 496 of 1965 is erroneous.

On 03 July 1986, the State of Andhra Pradesh in the Department of Revenue (J) issued a memorandum, Memo No. 609/J-2/81-27, stating therein that the land-holders of Vuyyur and Meduru estates cannot contend that the decision of the Supreme Court in Venkatagiri's case, does not bind them merely because appeals were not filed against the judgment in their favour and the law declared by the Supreme Court is binding on the land-holders whether they were parties to the Judgment or not.

The respondents herein filed a writ petition, which was registered as Writ Petition No. 16737 of 1990, claiming interim payments from 01 July 1964 to 31 November 1970 and to implement the earlier order in their favour passed by the High Court.

The learned Single Judge by Judgment dated 30th of January, 1993, dismissed the writ petition on the ground that the very basis namely the judgment in Venkatagiri's case, having been set aside by the Supreme Court, the earlier decision in favour of the respondents would not constitute an enforceable right and as such a writ of mandamus cannot be issued.

The respondents however assailed the aforesaid judgment of the learned Single Judge in writ appeal No. 511 of 1993 and the said writ appeal having been allowed, the present appeal has been preferred by the State Government by grant of special leave.
issues: What is the effect of the Supreme Court's judgment in Venkatagiri's case on the respondents' claim for interim payments?
Is the Division Bench of the Andhra Pradesh High Court correct in issuing a mandamus contrary to the declaration of law made by the Supreme Court in Venkatagiri's case?
Can the respondents rely on the earlier judgment in their favour, despite the Supreme Court having set aside that judgment in Venkatagiri's case?
petitioner_arguments: The law declared by the Supreme Court in the appeal in the case of State of Andhra Pradesh & Ors. vs. Venkatagiri & Ors. is the law of the land and binding on all persons throughout the country in view of Art. 141 of the Constitution.
The Division Bench of the High Court committed serious error in issuing a mandamus contrary to the declaration of law made by the Supreme Court in Venkatagiri's case.

The very Judgment in favour of the respondents having emanated, because of the Judgment of Andhra Pradesh High Court in Venkatagiri's case and the judgment of Venkatagiri, having been set aside, the respondents cannot make any claim on the basis of the earlier judgment in their favour.
respondent_arguments: The respondents are entitled to receive interim payments in accordance with the judgments in their favour.
The Division Bench of the High Court is correct in issuing a mandamus to make interim payments to the respondents herein in accordance with law laid down in Venkatagiri's case.
The respondents' claim for interim payments from 01 July 1964 to 31 November 1970 and to implement the earlier order in their favour passed by the High Court is valid.
court_reasoning: The Supreme Court held that the amendment of 1971 Act is valid and it having further held that the period during which the interim payments are payable under the Act ends with the date of original determination made by the Director u/s. 39(1) of the Act.
The Division Bench of the High Court committed serious error in issuing a mandamus contrary to the declaration of law made by the Supreme Court in Venkatagiri's case.
The respondents cannot make any claim on the basis of the earlier judgment in their favour, as that judgment was set aside by the Supreme Court.
holding: The appeal is allowed and the impugned Judgment of the Division Bench of the Andhra Pradesh High Court dated 04 November 1993 in Writ Appeal No. 511 of 1993 is set aside.
The respondents are not entitled to receive interim payments from 01 July 1964 to 31 November 1970 and to implement the earlier order in their favour passed by the High Court.
The law declared by the Supreme Court in Venkatagiri's case is the law of the land and binding on all persons throughout the country in view of Art. 141 of the Constitution.
